plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to eliminate that risk.
Reduce broad index (SPY) to 20% to free up capital and reduce concentration.
Increase allocation to income ETF (QQQI) to 15% for stability.
Trim high-conviction tech (CRWD) to 10% to lower single-name risk.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation with a significant cash buffer.
conservative.read: This conservative approach aims for lower, steadier returns around 1.5% per month. The focus is on reducing risk and preserving capital, accepting lower growth potential.

plan: Slightly reduce leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to 3% and 2% respectively.
Trim broad index (SPY) to 25% to address concentration and create buffer.
Initiate a small position in an inverse ETF (SOXS) for downside protection.
Reduce income ETF (QQQI) to 10% to reallocate capital.
This plan balances risk reduction with modest growth opportunities.
balanced.read: This balanced strategy targets around 2.5% per month by managing risk first. It aims to reduce concentration and leverage while adding a hedge, accepting moderate growth.

plan: Increase leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to 6% each, leaning into volatility.
Add a significant position in an inverse ETF (SOXS) at 6% for hedging.
Increase allocation to strong performer (CRWD) to 20% for concentrated growth.
Initiate a new position in a high-potential tech name (META) at 10%.
This aggressive plan seeks high returns but accepts significantly higher risk and drawdown.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month by embracing leverage and concentration. Expect amplified gains and losses, with leveraged ETFs decaying daily and higher drawdown potential.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to remove volatility.
Reduce broad index (SPY) to 20% to increase cash for income generation.
Significantly increase income ETF (QQQI) to 30% for steady distributions.
Sell high-beta tech (CRWD) and sector ETF (SMH) to cut risk.
This plan prioritizes consistent monthly income and low drawdown over growth.
income.read: This income-focused strategy aims for around 1% per month through distributions. It prioritizes capital preservation and steady cash flow, accepting minimal growth potential.
